prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: checked baggage from acceptance (bag-drop/transfer induction) through screening, sorting, make-up, to handoff at outbound load control point. Elements: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (records accepted bag; sends Oversize Exception Ticket); Bag Tag Printer (tag with unique identifier); Transfer Bag Feeder (records transfer bags; sends Late Transfer Bag Card); Induction Tray Conveyor (controlled spacing to screening for image capture); Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (associates tag with passenger/flight record; checks flight open/record complete; validates transfer routing; applies approved screening profile from tag data and operating configuration; routes exception bags to Secondary Inspection Chute avoiding outbound flows); Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (grants induction permissive; produces Recovery Route Card); Flight Data Gateway (flight/routing records; sends Flight Cutoff Advisory); Primary Crossbelt Sorter, alias Juniper (receives inducted bags, maintains identity, routes per active routing data and screening disposition); North Gate Scanner, alias Kestrel (reads bag identifier at network entry); South Gate Scanner (independent read point; produces Manual Rescan Receipt); both scanners acquire screening images, return disposition, record image quality/alarm status; Image Resolution Desk (staff assess unresolved images using full image, bag ID, prompts; record disposition); Secondary Inspection Chute (occupancy monitored); Bag Reconciliation Station; East/West Make-Up Conveyor; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit; Outbound Load Control Desk. Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor; Explosives Response Team; Security Duty Manager; Maintenance Technician; Airline Ramp Coordinator (sends Carousel Release Slip when outbound build authorized); staff. Items: bag tag/identifier, checked baggage, screening images, disposition, Flight Cutoff Advisory, Recovery Route Card, Oversize Exception Ticket, Late Transfer Bag Card, Manual Rescan Receipt, Carousel Release Slip, flight/routing records, induction permissive, equipment status, screening profile. States: clear, exception status, awaiting review. Requirements: hold bags with missing/conflicting data and oversized bags until route confirmed; induction needs valid record, route, ready equipment; interlocks stop feed on jam, door opening, downstream readiness loss; incomplete exam never treated as clear; awaiting-review bags under controlled routing, barred from make-up; clear permits normal routing only if identity and screening record agree; alarm/unresolved/missing record → exception status; no release into blocked chute position.

New part:
S066: Access to the Secondary Inspection Chute and its associated work area is limited to personnel with authorized duties.
S067: Explosives Response Team responds to escalated alarms and coordinates any required safety controls with airport security personnel.
S068: In local radio traffic, Explosives Response Team is also called Pebble.
S069: Inspection staff maintain physical control of an alarmed bag and do not return it to the sorter until an authorized disposition is recorded.
S070: The Bag Reconciliation Station verifies that the bag presented for examination matches the screening record before further handling.
S071: If an examination requires the bag to remain isolated, staff secure the area and notify the Baggage Operations Supervisor.
S072: The Baggage Operations Supervisor coordinates decisions that affect flight readiness, staffing, or continued operation of a screening lane.
S073: The Security Duty Manager is notified when an alarm response requires a security decision beyond routine screening procedures.
S074: The Bag Tag Printer produces a Calibration Witness Tag when a calibration witness record is required.
S075: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit is also known locally as Orchard.
S076: The Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit accepts only bags with a valid screening disposition and an authorized routing instruction.
S077: The Transfer Bag Feeder holds transfer bags from release until their screening status and intended onward handling are confirmed.
S078: Staff return a bag to normal handling only after its identity, examination outcome, and routing authorization are consistent in the operating record.
S079: The Baggage Control System loads the approved sort plan and applies its effective time window before bags enter sortation.
S080: Lantern is the operational alias used for the Flight Data Gateway in sortation coordination.
S081: The Baggage Control System checks the plan against current flight and handling records before assigning a route.
S082: The Concourse Zone Controller coordinates local conveyor availability with the active sort plan.
S083: The Induction Tray Conveyor presents bags at controlled spacing so each bag can be identified before route selection.
S084: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter applies the assigned destination and screening status to each identified bag.
S085: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter sends a Chute Occupancy Note when a destination lane approaches its configured limit.
S086: Route selection favors the approved path with adequate capacity and sufficient time for the planned handling.
S087: The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner verify bag identity at their respective route decision points.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
